RAJYA  SABHA
————
List of Questions for ORAL ANSWERS
to be asked at a sitting of the Rajya Sabha to be held on
Thursday,  the December 11, 2008/Agrahayana 20, 1930 (Saka)
————
(Ministries: Prime Minister; Atomic Energy; Coal; Communications and
Information Technology; Development of North Eastern Region;
Environment and Forests; External Affairs; Housing and
Urban Poverty Alleviation; Information and Broadcasting;
Overseas Indian Affairs; Panchayati Raj; Parliamentary
Affairs; Personnel, Public Grievances and Pensions;
Planning; Shipping, Road Transport and Highways;
Space; Statistics and Programme Implementation;
Urban Development; Y outh Affairs and Sports)
Total number of questions — 20
49
3G spectrum bids
*141. SHRI VIJAY JAW AHARLAL
DARDA:
SHRI GIREESH KUMAR
SANGHI:
Will the Minister of
COMMUNICATIONS AND
INFORMATION TECHNOLOGY be
pleased to state:
(a) whether his Ministry  has delayed
3G spectrum bids considerably;
(b) if so, whether  the Ministry of
Finance has also urged his Ministry to hold
auction  as early as possible so that the
estimated Rs. 40,000 crores can be
budgeted in the current fiscal books to
bridge the fiscal deficit;
(c) if so, whether  a number of political
parties have also criticised Government over
the favouring of chosen corporates;
(d) if so, whether  the new 3G telecom
is to share a 3 per cent  revenue with
Government; and
(e) if so, by what time a final decision in
this regard is likely to be taken?
Scheme for urban transport planning
*142. SHRI GIREESH KUMAR
SANGHI:
DR. T. SUBBARAMI
REDDY:
Will the Minister of URBAN
DEVELOPMENT be pleased to state:
(a) whether Government  is likely to
launch a Rs. 152 crore scheme for urban
transport planning to encourage States to
upgrade public transport systems which are
crumbling in most cities including the
Metros;
(b) if so, whether  his Ministry's
programme  that  is aimed at promoting  eco-
friendly, safe, comfortable and affordable
public transport would push cities to take
up  studies to prepare detailed project
reports after comprehensive and thorough
evaluation of alternate technologies;

50
(c) if so, whether his Ministry has
already started studies in this regard; and
(d) if so, by what time a final decision
in this regard is likely to be taken?
National  Urban Poor Fund
*143. SHRIMATI T. RA TNA BAI:
Will the Minister of HOUSING  AND
URBAN POVERTY ALLEVIATION be
pleased to state:
(a) whether Government is setting up a
National Urban Poor Fund;
(b) if so, the details thereof and the
purpose behind it;
(c) whether the master plans had
neglected the needs of the informal sector,
which engages 92 per cent of the total
workforce in cities and towns, especially
in the coastal areas of Andhra Pradesh;
(d) if so, the details thereof; and
(e) the steps to be taken in this
direction?
Dialogue with Foreign Minister of
Pakistan
*144. SHRIMATI  SUPRIYA SULE:
SHRI GIREESH KUMAR
SANGHI:
Will the Minister of EXTERNAL
AFFAIRS be pleased to state:
(a) whether  Foreign Ministers of India
and Pakistan met in May, 2008 to continue
the unfinished dialogue;
(b) if so, whether there was also a
meeting on Indo-Pak anti-terror mechanism
in the month of October, 2008;
(c) if so, the main subjects discussed
thereat;
(d) whether  any agreement in regard to
meeting the threat of terror has been reached;
(e) if so, to what extent  both countries
have implemented the proposals; and
(f) to what extent  anti-terror mechanism
of India and Pakistan has been successful?
Gap in consumption-expenditure
†*145. SHRI RAM JETH-
MALANI: Will the PRIME MINISTER
be pleased to state:
(a) whether  it is a fact that  there is a
huge difference  in the consumption-
expenditure of the people living in the rural
and urban areas of the country;
(b) if so, the amount of monthly
expenditure on consumption, respectively,
by the people living in the rural and urban
areas during the years 2006 to 2008; and
(c) the details of this expenditure during
the years 1990 to 1992?
Funds for National Highway projects
*146. SHRI V . HANUMANTHA
RAO:
DR. T. SUBBARAMI
REDDY:
Will the Minister of SHIPPING, ROAD
TRANSPORT AND HIGHWAYS be
pleased to state:
(a) whether in order to attract
companies to invest in Highway projects,
his Ministry has approached  the Finance
Ministry seeking low cost funds;
(b) whether  a special window from the
RBI that  would provide  for extension of
reasonable interest rates for highway
projects was also considered;
(c) if so, the projects that are being
delayed due to want  of funds  and to what
†Original notice of the question received in Hindi.

51
extent Government has agreed to provide
funds to these projects;
(d) by what time they are likely to be
completed;
(e) whether  National Highways
Authority of India  has agreed to abandon
two projects at Vijayawada and
Machilipatnam; and
(f) if so, the  reasons therefor?
Discussion to counter terrorism
*147. SHRI JESUDASU SEELAM:
Will the Minister of EXTERNAL
AFFAIRS be pleased to state:
(a) whether  Governments of India and
Nepal have  met and discussed  the steps
to counter-terror;
(b) if so, the main points discussed;
(c) whether effective cooperation for
combating terrorist activities, including the
activities of the Indian Insurgent Group
operating from Nepal and the Himalayan
nation being  used as a major transit point
for circulation of fake Indian currency notes
in India, were also  discussed;
(d) if so, the outcome of the talks held;
and
(e) to what extent India and Nepal have
taken steps to check the terror activities in
both the countries?
Coal shortage in NTPC
*148. DR. T. SUBBARAMI REDDY:
Will the PRIME MINISTER be pleased to
state:
(a) whether there is a coal shortage in
the country and National Thermal Power
Corporation (NTPC) and State  Power
firms have approached  his Ministry to
meet the shortage of coal in power projects;
(b) whether all the power projects have
been facing coal  shortage;
(c) whether the Board of Coal India Ltd.
has approved a first ever proposal to import
coal;
(d) if so, the total coal to be imported;
(e) the total requirements; and
(f) to what extent import  of coal would
meet the shortage?
Marine Emergency Relief Fund
*149. SHRI M.V. MYSURA REDDY:
Will the Minister of SHIPPING, ROAD
TRANSPORT AND  HIGHW AYS be
pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that  the number
of marine casualties, loss of ships in the
Indian territorial waters etc. have gone up
in the last few years;
(b) if so, whether  it is a fact that his
Ministry has decided to create Marine
Emergency Relief Fund to address the
above and other issues;
(c) whether it is also a fact that a
Committee of Experts has been set up to
look into all these aspects; and
(d) if so, the details of recommendations
made by the Committee?
Land management in major ports
*150. SHRI RAJEEV SHUKLA: Will
the Minister of SHIPPING, ROAD
TRANSPORT AND HIGHWAYS be
pleased to state:
(a) whether  he has written to the Indian
Ports Association to prepare a
comprehensive information system on land
management pattern in major ports of the
country;
(b) if so, whether response has been
received from the association;

52
(c) if so, the concrete measures and
steps his Ministry is considering to take to
improve the major ports in the country;
(d) whether  all the State Governments
concerned have  to provide  more  land, etc.
for development of ports; and
(e) whether the Union Government  has
approved Rs. 1008 crores for development
of these projects?
National Highway Development in
NER
*151. SHRI BIRENDRA PRASAD
BAISHYA: Will the Minister of
SHIPPING, ROAD TRANSPORT AND
HIGHWAYS be pleased to state:
(a) whether  it is a fact that Union
Government is planning to spend
Rs. 25,000 crore for  development of
National Highways in North Eastern Region
(NER);
(b) if so, the details and the break up
thereof, sector-wise;
(c) whether  it is a fact that the proposed
four-lane highway under State Capital
Connectivity is yet to  materialize;
(d) if so, the details and the reasons
therefor;
(e) if not, the factual status thereof,
sector-wise;
(f) whether  some part of the proposed
four-lane road is planned keeping two lanes
apart with a gap of 1 km.; and
(g) if so, the reasons therefor?
Stamp on Kalagura Bishnu Prasad
Rabha
*152. KUMAR DEEPAK DAS: Will
the Minister of COMMUNICATIONS
AND INFORMATION TECHNOLOGY
be pleased to state:
(a) whether  Government has assured
that release of postal stamp of Kalagura
Bishnu Prasad Rabha during his Birth
centenary is under process;
(b) whether Government has taken any
steps to release  such a postal stamp  by
20th January, the last day of centenary
celebration; and
(c) if not, the reasons therefor?
Salary to coaches and selectors
*153. SHRI N.R. GOVINDARAJAR:
Will the Minister of YOUTH AFFAIRS
AND SPORTS be pleased to state:
(a) whether  coaches and selectors of
Hockey hold honorary positions and are
not entitled for salary for their services;
(b) if so, the details thereof; and
(c) whether there is any proposal to
pay coaches and selectors as per foreign
model where coaches are paid and treated
as professionals and make them more
responsible and accountable?
Energy generating plants
†*154. DR. MURLI MANOHAR
JOSHI:
SHRI SHIV ANAND TIWARI:
Will the PRIME MINISTER be pleased
to state:
(a) whether  it is a fact that the atomic
energy generating plants in the country had
been generating energy below their installed
capacity on account of non-availability of
uranium for last few years;
(b) if so, the details thereof;
(c) the percentage of capacity utilised
during the years 2005-06, 2006-07 and
2007-08, respectively; and
†Original notice of the question received in Hindi.

53
(d) the respective percentage of the
escalation of production costs due to under
utilisation of the capacity?
Funds for production of uranium
†*155. SHRI SHIVANAND TIWARI:
SHRI RAM JETHMALANI:
Will the PRIME MINISTER be pleased
to state:
(a) whether  it is a fact that Government
has allocated Rs. 700 crores to 800 crores
under the  Eleventh Plan to enhance the
production of uranium in the country;
(b) if so, the details thereof and the
separate percentage of plan and non-plan
expenditure out of the allocation; and
(c) the volume of domestic  production
of uranium in the country at the end of
Eleventh Plan after the said expenditure
and the extent by which it would exceed
the production of the year 2004-05?
Cost overruns
*156. SHRI DARA SINGH: Will the
Minister of STATISTICS AND
PROGRAMME IMPLEMENTATION
be pleased to state:
(a) whether  according to his Ministry’s
Report on the status of Central
Government, 897 infrastructure projects
worth Rs. 3,59,451 crore, surveyed
between July and September, 2007 shows
that 318 projects are running behind
schedule;
(b) whether it is a fact that as on
30th September, 2007 delayed projects
witnessed cost overruns of 15.32 per cent,
thereby increasing  the cost by Rs. 24,670
crore;
(c) if so,  the reasons for huge cost
overrun of 318 delayed projects, Sector-
wise and location-wise; and
(d) the steps taken by Government to
reduce/minimise additional burden on
exchequer in this regard?
People above poverty line
†*157. SHRI RAJ MOHINDER
SINGH MAJITHA:
DR. MURLI MANOHAR
JOSHI:
Will the PRIME MINISTER be pleased
to state:
(a) whether  it is a fact that a person
earning more than Rs. 456 per month in the
country is being considered living above
the poverty line by Government;
(b) if so, the facts thereof;
(c) the basis formulated by Government
to determine the said norm; and
(d) the number of persons  being
considered living above the poverty line at
present on the basis of said norm?
Code to regulate advertisements
*158. SHRI KAMAL AKHTAR:
SHRI JAI PARKASH
AGGARW AL:
Will the Minister of INFORMATION
AND BROADCASTING  be pleased to
state:
(a) whether  Government proposes to
introduce a new code to regulate the
contents of advertisements so that there is
no adverse effect of any kind on the children
in the country;
(b) if so, the details thereof;
(c) whether Advertising Standards
Council of India has examined or is
examining  this issue;
(d) if so, the details thereof; and
(e) the outcome of such a study?
†Original notice of the question received in Hindi.

54
Swan Telecom
*159. SHRI DHARAM PAL
SABHARWAL: W ill the Minister of
COMMUNICATIONS AND
INFORMATION TECHNOLOGY be
pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a  fact that  Government
has given licence to Swan Telecom under
the "first come first serve" basis;
(b) if so, the details of policy under
which the licence was given with fee charged
from the company;
(c) the equity pattern of the Swan
Telecom as per the Memorandum of
Association on the date of licence on "first
come first serve’’  basis;
(d) whether  grant of licence to the
company is a violation of clause 8 of the
guidelines for Unified Access Service
Licence; and
(e) if so, the details thereof and action
taken against the company for violation of
above rule?
N
EW DELHI; V . K. AGNIHOTRI,
The 5th December, 2008 Secretary-General.
Agrahayana 14, 1930 (Saka)
2G spectrum licence
*160. SHRI R.C. SINGH: Will the
Minister of COMMUNICATIONS AND
INFORMATION TECHNOLOGY be
pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that the private
parties who were allotted 2G Spectrum
licence, sold their stake to foreign players
at huge premium, allegedly at a huge loss
to the exchequer;
(b) if so, who are these private players,
at what price they were allotted the
spectrum and at what price their stake was
sold to the foreign companies;
(c) whether the spectrum allotment
policy of Government is the reason for the
huge loss of revenue to the exchequer in
this respect; and
(d) if so, the corrective measures being
taken in this regard?
